questions.question: What is the primary role of the <picture> element in modern HTML?
options: To provide art direction and next-gen format fallbacks (AVIF/WebP)
questions.hint: Format fallbacks and media-based art direction.
questions.explanation: <picture> wraps <source> tags to provide format negotiation (AVIF -> WebP -> JPEG) and art direction.

questions.question: What happens if you omit the element inside a wrapper?
options: Nothing is displayed; the image fails to render completely
The browser defaults to a generic blue box
It downloads all sources at once
questions.explanation: The element is mandatory inside ; without it, no image will be drawn to the screen.

questions.question: In a srcset attribute (e.g. srcset="pic.jpg 800w"), what does the '800w' represent?
options: The intrinsic image width in pixels
The maximum viewport width in CSS pixels
questions.explanation: The 'w' unit describes the true intrinsic width of the image asset in raw pixels.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the sizes attribute when used with srcset?
options: It scales the user font size
It tells the browser what width the image will occupy in the layout before CSS downloads
questions.hint: It informs the browser of the display slot size.
questions.explanation: The sizes attribute declares the expected display width of the image at various breakpoints, enabling early source selection.

questions.question: Which image format offers the highest compression efficiency for photographic content in modern browsers?
questions.explanation: AVIF delivers state-of-the-art compression efficiency, producing significantly smaller files than JPEG and WebP.
